name: Launch Customer Replied → Conversation AI (SMS + Chat)
spec_ref: launch-automations.spec.md §3.4 — Conversation AI (Skill 38, optional, through the 44 + 38 TRINITY)

supporting: GoHighLevel help — Customer Replied trigger (filters by channel, message direction (inbound), phrase, tag, intent)
GoHighLevel help — Conversation AI workflow action (talks, waits for replies, branches booked / answered / timed out)
GoHighLevel help — Update Conversation AI Bot and Status (keyword wake-up)

applicability.requested: The launch intake answers 'Conversation AI: yes'. Build this workflow, and Skill 38 writes the playbook in the same unit (TRINITY).
applicability.not_requested: Do nothing and build nothing. The launch package must record the literal line: `Conversation AI: not requested`. Do NOT pass `--conversational` to `qc-built-workflow.sh` — that flag hard-gates WF-19 against the Skill 38 TRINITY registry, which has no row for a launch that never asked for a bot.

purpose: When a launch contact replies to a text (SMS) or a web chat, the Conversation AI bot answers their question from the approved offer facts, books the call when they ask for one, or sends the checkout link when they are ready to buy. The workflow then sorts the reply into one of three outcomes — booked, answered, timed out — so each outcome gets its own follow-up. A keyword (for example 'HELP' or 'CALL') wakes the bot again through Update Conversation AI Bot and Status. Skill 44 builds the workflow; Skill 38 writes the bot playbook. Neither ships alone.

trinity.rule: GHL workflow + communications playbook + workflow-AI prompt travel together as ONE unit. The visual travels too (Skill 38 workflow-visual-protocol).

who_builds_what.skill_44: This workflow: trigger, Conversation AI action, branches, keyword wake-up, tags.
who_builds_what.skill_38: The playbook text, the Build-with-AI prompt, the visual, and the registry row in the client's `conversation-workflows/registry.md`.

checkers_each_runs: Skill 44 side: `qc-built-workflow.sh <workflow-id> --conversational` runs Skill 38's `qc-trinity-registry.sh` as a HARD gate. WF-19 fails mechanically on a non-zero trinity exit.
Skill 38 side: `scripts/11-run-qc-checklist.sh` re-runs `qc-trinity-registry.sh` over the registry.
A registry row whose Layer 1 is 'No (uses existing inbound routing)' is legitimately prompt-free and passes.
trinity.fail_closed: No playbook registered → no Build-with-AI prompt → WF-19 fails → the workflow is NOT done, even if the GHL build succeeded.

trigger.name: Customer Replied
trigger.what_starts_it: An inbound message from the contact on a watched channel during the launch window.

default_config.channels: SMS + Chat only. Email replies are out of scope for this template.
default_config.filter: Apply Channel first, then Message Direction = Inbound. Without the inbound-direction guard, the workflow can re-trigger on the bot's own outbound message, creating a runaway loop. No further filter narrows replies by default; the bot answers every launch reply. Narrow it only when the owner asks (for example, tag `launch-2026` so unrelated threads never enter).
default_config.reentry: Once per contact per launch unless the owner asks for separate instances; re-entry guarded by tag `ZHC-launch-ai-replied`.

trigger.engine_note: CampaignBuilder auto-creates ONLY a Tag Added trigger. Customer Replied must be installed with `caf workflows patch-trigger --workflow-id <id> --trigger-json <file>` (internal API, pre-write snapshot captured automatically), or through the Tier-4 managed browser when no verified trigger payload exists. The exact internal `type` string for Customer Replied is NOT verified in the engine source — read the live definition with `caf workflows get` / a snapshot first and reuse the observed shape. Never invent the enum.

what_the_bot_answers_from: Offer name, price, what is included, who it is for
Launch dates: doors open, doors close, delivery/access date
Booking link (calendar) for the sales call
Payment plan availability (only when the offer has plans)
A2P status: if registration is not approved, SMS replies cannot go out — say so in the playbook
prohibited: No invented discounts, bonuses, dates or guarantees
No medical, legal or financial advice beyond approved copy
No promises about outcomes the offer does not state
offer_facts.ownership: Skill 38 owns the playbook wording. Skill 44 only wires the node and its branches.

sequence.detail: Contact replies during the launch. Re-entry guard: tag `ZHC-launch-ai-replied` absent.
sequence.parallel: Underlying send workflow (texts/emails) keeps running — this workflow does not stop promotional sends.

sequence.detail: Route the reply into the Conversation AI action. The action talks, waits for the contact's next message, and reads the playbook (Skill 38) for answers drawn from the offer facts.
intents_the_bot_handles: Question about the offer → answer from offer facts, then re-invite the next step
Wants to talk → offer the booking link and hold the thread open
Ready to buy → send the checkout link
Not interested / stop → honor it, tag `ZHC-launch-ai-optout`, end

sequence.detail: The Conversation AI action resolves into exactly one of three outcomes; each gets its own follow-up path below.

sequence.beat: Keyword wake-up — Update Conversation AI Bot and Status
sequence.detail: When the contact sends the wake keyword (default `CALL`, configurable) — even after the bot went quiet or timed out — this action re-activates the bot on that conversation and resumes the same playbook.
sequence.placement: After the timed-out branch and as a standing listener for the keyword on the launch channels.

booked.signal: Conversation AI outcome = Appointment booked (or the booking tag/pipeline stage the owner uses)
actions: Remove from the launch AI re-invite path
Create/update opportunity at the booked stage (if the launch pipeline exists)
Send the approved confirmation message with date, time and timezone
Notify the owner (internal notification) with the contact name and booking time
booked.exit: Exit to the owner's call-reminder / show-up workflow if one exists. Do not keep selling in this thread.

answered.signal: Conversation AI outcome = question answered, no booking and no purchase
actions: Leave the contact in the promotional launch sequence (do not exit it)
Resume the next scheduled promo touch; the bot stays available for further replies
answered.exit: The workflow stays listening. A later booking moves the contact to the booked branch on the same thread.

timed_out.signal: Conversation AI outcome = timed out (contact went quiet before the exchange finished)
actions: Wait the owner-approved duration (default 1 day; duration Wait, never an event Wait)
Send ONE short approved nudge with the booking link and/or checkout link
If still no reply → tag `ZHC-launch-ai-dormant` and stop; the keyword wake-up remains the only re-entry
timed_out.rules: One nudge. Never a drip. Launch promo sends are capped at 3–5 per launch and this nudge counts toward that cap.

keyword_wake_up.action: Update Conversation AI Bot and Status
keyword_wake_up.behavior: Keyword arrival re-opens (or keeps open) the bot on that conversation and sets status active, so the playbook answers again — this is the only path back for a `ZHC-launch-ai-dormant` contact.
keyword_wake_up.cap: Once per contact per day; ignore repeats beyond that.
keyword_wake_up.stop_words: STOP/UNSUBSCRIBE and any owner-defined opt-out always win over the keyword wake-up.

dependencies_first.note: caf refuses/loses work if these do not exist. Create BEFORE the workflow, and read backs are required.
dependencies_first.conversation_ai_agent: Create with the official Conversation AI API — `POST /conversation-ai/agents` and `POST /conversation-ai/agents/{agentId}/actions` (Version 2021-04-15, scope conversation-ai.write). This is the one launch family with a public write path for the bot itself.
dependencies_first.calendar: The booking calendar must already exist (public API can create one: `POST /calendars/`).
dependencies_first.a2p: If A2P 10DLC is not approved, the SMS channel is draft-only. Build it, and the launch package carries the warning: texts cannot send until A2P is approved.

workflow.trigger: Customer Replied — channels SMS + Chat, Message Direction = Inbound, re-entry guarded by tag `ZHC-launch-ai-replied`. Install via `caf workflows patch-trigger` after reading the live trigger shape.
workflow.build_path: `caf --experimental workflows create --name '<Launch> Customer Replied AI' --folder '<Launch>' --from-json <campaign.json>`. `create-step` covers only email / sms / wait / tag / webhook / ai — the Conversation AI node and Update Conversation AI Bot and Status node are written as raw step objects in the campaign JSON.
nodes: Trigger: Customer Replied (SMS + Chat; Message Direction = Inbound)
If/Else: tag `ZHC-launch-ai-optout` present? Yes → Stop. No → continue
Action: Conversation AI (agent = the launch agent; playbook = Skill 38's registered playbook) — waits for the contact's reply
Branch: outcome booked → tag `ZHC-launch-ai-booked`; confirmation message; opportunity stage update; internal notification → Stop
Branch: outcome answered → tag `ZHC-launch-ai-answered` → Stop (promo sequence continues outside this workflow)
Branch: outcome timed out → tag `ZHC-launch-ai-timed-out` → Wait 1 day (duration) → SMS nudge with `{{booking_link}}` / `{{checkout_link}}` → Wait 1 day → tag `ZHC-launch-ai-dormant` → Stop
Action: Update Conversation AI Bot and Status (keyword `{{wake_keyword}}`, default CALL) — re-activates the bot and sets status active
if_else_branches: Opt-out guard first: `ZHC-launch-ai-optout` present → Stop, never answer
Outcome switch on the Conversation AI action: booked / answered / timed out
Wake keyword guard: keyword present and contact not opted out and last wake > 24h → re-activate
A2P guard on the timed-out nudge: SMS only when A2P is approved; otherwise the nudge is recorded as a draft and the branch tags `ZHC-launch-ai-nudge-blocked`
skill44_notes: Set every node's `order` and `parentKey` BEFORE the first save (Skill 44 reliability rule).

`conversation_ai` is in `VERIFIED_ACTIONS` — the action type is verified, but there is NO builder helper for it, so it goes in as a raw step object. Verify the saved shape with `caf workflows export` before claiming done.

`Update Conversation AI Bot and Status` is NOT in `VERIFIED_ACTIONS`. Do not invent a type string: build it through the Tier-4 managed browser, or read an existing definition from the location and reuse the observed payload. If neither is available, report that specific unfinished node — never report the workflow complete.
CampaignBuilder writes DRAFTS only; triggers stay inactive while `CAF_DRAFT_ONLY` is set. Nothing goes live in this lane.
Take a pre-write snapshot before every patch (`patch-trigger`, `update`, `patch-email` capture one automatically).

qc.must_show: Every branch present by read-back, the Conversation AI node's agent id correct, the keyword node present, and the Skill 38 registry row complete.

flexibility.core_principle: A guide and a resource, never a rule. The owner's own wording, channels and keyword win at every level.
overridable: Whether a timed-out contact gets a nudge at all
Whether the bot books, sends checkout, or only answers questions
flexibility.never: Never build this workflow when the intake said no. Never ship the workflow without the Skill 38 playbook. Never answer from facts the owner did not approve.
